test_title: PYST 22: Selection Post (Graduate Level) - English Language (Held On 24 Jul, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

The security protocols had been overlooked by the administration prior to the incident.

options.text: The administration has overlooked the security protocols prior to the incident.
The administration overlooks the security protocols prior to the incident.
The administration was overlooking the security protocols prior to the incident.
The administration had overlooked the security protocols prior to the incident.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The original sentence is in the **Past Perfect Passive** voice ("had been overlooked").
 
• To convert this to the **active voice**, the agent performing the action ("the administration") becomes the subject of the sentence.
 
• The verb must remain in the **Past Perfect** tense. The passive structure *had + been + V3* changes to the active structure **had + V3**.
 
• Consequently, "had been overlooked" is converted to "**had overlooked**."

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The administration **had overlooked** the security protocols prior to the incident."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "The administration has overlooked..."** – This uses the Present Perfect tense, which incorrectly shifts the timeline to the present.
 
• **Option 2: "The administration overlooks..."** – This uses the Simple Present tense, which describes a general habit or fact rather than a past event.
 
• **Option 3: "The administration was overlooking..."** – This uses the Past Continuous tense, which describes an ongoing action in the past rather than a completed state/action.
